NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the apex of the AI accelerator value chain, acting as a fabless semiconductor designer that is critically dependent on TSMC for cutting-edge wafer fabrication and on SK Hynix/Micron for scarce HBM memory capacity. On the demand side, NVIDIA's revenue is overwhelmingly driven by a concentrated group of hyperscalers and cloud providers—Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and Meta—who are racing to build out AI infrastructure at unprecedented scale, making NVIDIA both enormously powerful and exposed to the capital expenditure cycles of a handful of customers.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the apex of the consumer electronics supply chain as a fabless designer that orchestrates a vast global network of semiconductor, display, and component suppliers — most critically TSMC for leading-edge chip fabrication — while distributing finished products through carriers, retailers, and its own direct channels worldwide. Its downstream relationships are increasingly dominated by high-margin services revenue, including the landmark Google search deal and App Store commissions, making Apple both a product company and a powerful platform gatekeeper.

TSM.supply_chain_summary: TSMC occupies the most strategically critical position in the global semiconductor supply chain as the world's dominant pure-play foundry, manufacturing chips designed by fabless companies and IDMs on leading-edge nodes that no other foundry can replicate at scale. Its upstream dependencies on a small set of highly specialized equipment suppliers (particularly ASML's monopoly on EUV) and its downstream concentration among a handful of mega-cap technology customers create significant interdependencies that make TSMC both indispensable and exposed to geopolitical and supply disruption risks.

On the demand side, Micron's revenue is increasingly driven by AI infrastructure buildout — particularly HBM shipments to NVIDIA — alongside diversified exposure to hyperscalers, mobile OEMs, and automotive/embedded markets.

OKLO.supply_chain_summary: Oklo sits at an early-stage, critical junction in the advanced fission value chain, dependent heavily on a narrow set of specialized upstream suppliers for HALEU fuel enrichment and nuclear-grade components — areas where supply constraints represent the primary execution risk. On the downstream side, Oklo is actively targeting power-hungry hyperscale data center operators and industrial customers seeking reliable, carbon-free baseload electricity, with Microsoft representing its most publicly confirmed customer relationship to date.
